note:
FEATURE / WORLDBUILDER / MACRO-WORLD PHYSICAL REALIZATION ISSUE: The recently completed `20260828-215100-000-KentridgeTopDownWorldLayout` established a source-backed semantic macro graph for the Mounting Force world (named settlements/regions, reserved envelopes, verified routes, provenance, deterministic placement) and a small top-down inspection overlay. That foundation is useful, but the actual 3D world still does not visibly realize enough of that graph. Loading `KentridgePlayableSlice` should not leave the player with a minimap that claims Moordell, Rossdam, Fairy Village, Orc Village, etc. exist while the world itself contains only sparse neutral markers. The next step is to make the macro definition drive an inspectable physical blockout of the larger world.

PRIMARY GOAL: Turn the existing macro-world graph into a real WorldBuilder-generated regional blockout. Every settlement node must have a visible physical settlement presence, verified connections between settlements/regions must produce continuous traversable roads or trails, and WorldBuilder must gain reusable high-level terrain-region authoring capable of expressing large geographic features such as lakes, mountain/ridge barriers, valleys/passes, plains/meadows, forests, and similar regional forms. These features must participate in placement and route solving rather than being decorative overlays.

REUSE THE EXISTING MACRO MODEL: Extend the production `TopDownWorldLayout` / `MountingForceTopDownWorldDefinition` / shared WorldBuilder path created by the prior issue. Do not replace it with a second scene-local map, hand-authored Unity transforms, or a Kentridge-only procedural generator. The existing verified hard topology remains authoritative. The macro graph should become the semantic input to physical terrain, route, and settlement-blockout generation. Preserve source/provenance distinctions from the prior issue and the original/imported Mounting Force references.

ROAD / TRAVEL NETWORK: The physical world must contain a readable road/trail network that follows the verified macro topology and connects the represented settlements. Every `TopDownWorldNodeKind.Settlement` must be physically reachable from Kentridge through contiguous generated travel surfaces corresponding to the hard-route graph. Roads must leave one settlement through a sensible edge/entrance, traverse the intervening regions, and arrive at the next settlement envelope; they may not terminate at a debug marker hundreds of metres away. Route geometry must be terrain-aware and walkable at gameplay scale. Avoid impossible slopes, deep-water crossings without an authored crossing solution, roads painted vertically up cliffs, self-intersections, settlement/building intersections, or disconnected tile gaps. When geography blocks a direct route, the WorldBuilder must be able to route around it or through an explicitly described solution such as a mountain pass, bridge/causeway, shoreline route, valley, tunnel-capable corridor reservation, or other semantic crossing.

SETTLEMENT BLOCKOUTS: Every settlement node in the macro graph must have more than a marker. For this issue, final town architecture and per-town art direction remain out of scope, but each settlement must generate a grounded, readable blockout with at least four building-scale structures (or the existing richer implementation when already available), an internal street/open-space arrangement, and a clear road arrival/exit. Existing Kentridge and Hightown generation should remain richer where already implemented; do not replace them with boxes. For currently unrealized destinations such as Moordell, Rossdam, Fairy Village, and Orc Village, simple reusable blockout buildings are acceptable as intentional layout instrumentation, but they must have believable scale, sit on terrain, avoid overlap, and read unmistakably as a settlement rather than four arbitrary cubes. The blockout system must be reusable for any settlement envelope and must not encode captured coordinates for specific towns. These placeholders are not final art and must be structured so later town-architecture work can replace/override them cleanly.

TOP-LEVEL TERRAIN / REGION AUTHORING CAPABILITY: Add or generalize a reusable WorldBuilder representation for large-scale geographic intent. It must be able to express, at minimum: (1) a named geographic feature/region kind such as lake/water body, mountain or ridge belt/barrier, valley/pass, plains/meadow, forest/woodland, and generic region; (2) approximate extent/footprint and elevation/depth intent rather than only a point marker; (3) semantic spatial relationships to settlements, routes, and other regions, including concepts such as `between`, `adjacent to`, `contains`, `separates`, `route passes through`, `route goes around`, and designated crossing/pass areas or an equivalent constraint model; (4) deterministic variation from a fixed seed; (5) terrain-shaping/output rules compatible with the existing voxel terrain/world-generation pipeline; and (6) enough query/constraint information for route solving and settlement placement to respect water, steep terrain, reserved envelopes, and crossings. Do not hard-code a single lake or mountain directly into `KentridgePlayableSlice`.

FIRST PHYSICAL GEOGRAPHY PASS: Use the legacy Mounting Force map/reference evidence where it provides useful macro composition guidance, while continuing to give verified traversal topology precedence. Where the source is ambiguous, create a deliberate modern 3D blockout rather than claiming invented geography is legacy fact. The built Kentridge macro world must include at least one substantial lake/water-body feature and at least one substantial mountain/ridge barrier authored through the new high-level region system. At least one of these features must visibly affect a hard travel route so the road demonstrably routes around, through, or across the geography using a semantic solution rather than ignoring it. Also realize broad regional terrain transitions so the space between towns reads as countryside/regions rather than an undifferentiated flat test plane. This ticket is about proving the authoring vocabulary and physical macro composition, not final biome dressing.

INTEGRATION WITH OTHER WORLDBUILDER SYSTEMS: The regional model should be the top-level source that later systems can consume. Roads/trails, settlement envelopes, vegetation/ecology policies, water, landmark placement, and future encounter/population systems should be able to query or compose against the same regional intent rather than each inventing an unrelated map. In particular, do not conflict with the separate Kentridge vegetation/meadow work: this issue should define where region kinds and exclusions are, while ecology density/species remain owned by the reusable ecology policy.

STREAMING / SCALE: This is a world-scale blockout, so do not eagerly instantiate every remote building as GameObjects or force the entire macro world into the highest-detail resident ring. Physical realization must remain compatible with the existing voxel streaming/LOD model. Settlement blockouts, roads, and terrain should stream deterministically from semantic definitions. Check generation time, route-solving cost, voxel/brick cost, far-field cost, memory, and rendering impact. Do not weaken existing device budgets to make the world visible.

VISUAL INSPECTION IS REQUIRED: This issue cannot close because the top-down overlay looks correct or because graph tests pass. Durable built-application evidence must show the actual physical world. Required evidence includes: (a) player-height views of continuous generated roads leaving and entering settlements; (b) a visible blockout settlement at every settlement node, with closer evidence for at least Moordell, Rossdam, Fairy Village, and Orc Village; (c) an elevated/top-down or survey view proving the physical road network corresponds to the semantic macro graph; (d) a substantial generated lake/water body and mountain/ridge feature; (e) a route visibly responding to one of those geographic constraints; and (f) normal CharacterMotor traversal on representative road segments with collision/streaming active. The debug minimap/overlay may remain useful instrumentation but is not itself acceptance evidence for physical realization.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) the existing source-backed Mounting Force macro graph remains the authoritative topology and is consumed through reusable WorldBuilder/shared-system APIs; (2) every settlement node has a physical generated settlement presence, with >=4 grounded reusable blockout buildings for destinations that do not yet have richer generation, plus internal circulation and a road arrival/exit; (3) every settlement is physically reachable from Kentridge through contiguous generated road/trail surfaces following the hard-route graph; (4) roads are terrain-aware, walkable, and do not silently cross lakes, cliffs, structures, or invalid slopes without a semantically authored crossing/routing solution; (5) WorldBuilder exposes reusable large-scale geographic-region authoring for at least lakes/water bodies, mountain/ridge barriers, valleys/passes, plains/meadows, forests/woodlands, extents/elevation intent, deterministic variation, relationships/constraints, and route/placement queries; (6) the exact built Kentridge macro world visibly contains at least one substantial lake and one substantial mountain/ridge feature authored through that system, with at least one hard route visibly altered or solved because of the geography; (7) regional terrain between towns reads as intentionally differentiated world space rather than a flat debug plane, without requiring final biome art; (8) no Kentridge-only direct voxel writing, giant static scene, hand-authored destination coordinates in the Unity hierarchy, or second independent world graph is introduced; (9) focused behavioral regressions exercise deterministic macro-to-physical realization, all-settlement reachability, continuous road generation, settlement blockout placement/non-overlap, geographic constraints, and a failure case proving an impossible blocked route is rejected or requires an explicit crossing/pass solution; (10) the exact built-application `KentridgePlayableSlice` reaches a usable rendered scene without startup/runtime exceptions and durable visual evidence demonstrates the physical settlements, roads, lake, mountains, constrained route, and representative real CharacterMotor traversal; and (11) blast radius and world-build/route-solving/CPU/GPU/memory/voxel-streaming cost are measured against existing budgets before closure.

NON-GOALS: final per-town architecture/material palettes; final decorative props; final NPC populations; final ecology/vegetation density (owned by the separate ecology ticket); exact reproduction of legacy TMX coordinates; replacing the existing Kentridge/Hightown detailed generators with blockouts; or treating the minimap as the delivered world.
resolutionSummary: Administratively closed at the user's explicit request: 'lets just close this scene issue. we can revisit later'. Deferred, not fixed or accepted. The last Kentridge acceptance replay still had missing published near-surface coverage at Moordell (jobs=8 missing=89), and visual/runtime/cost acceptance remains incomplete. Preserve the unchanged checklist and original criteria for an explicitly authorized revisit. This closure promotes documentation only; it does not ship or validate the unfinished implementation.
